title: Every plant and every animal, as a list you can click through
question: Clicking a row marks that individual in the box and puts its numbers on screen. Is the mark findable enough -- a bracket round a plant, a crosshair round a two-cell ant -- and are these the eight columns you would want to sort a hundred of them by?
context_md:
**What it does:** the box could tell you it held 52 ants and it could tell you about one ant, if you could spot it. This is the bit in between -- a roster of every individual, sorted and filtered, and a click that holds on to one.

**Where it sits:** first of four. Next is the genome read back in words instead of numbers, then a life record (age, offspring, feeding, cause of death), then side-by-side comparison and a lineage overlay.

**Reached from the PLANTS and ANTS pages**, not from the bar -- the bar is measured full, row 1 at exactly 508 of 508 pixels, so the way in is a LIST heading on the page those buttons already open.

**The pin is an identity, not a row and not a cell.** An ant walks out from under a cell inspector; a row number means a different animal the moment anything is born. Held across 240 ticks the pinned ant moved 13 cells and the page stayed on it.

**Two things I already found and fixed by looking at these:** every ant read HUNGRY (the threshold was scaled off what a corpse is worth, not what an animal lives on), and every ant read HOME (that constant is a 3,000-tick sense window, not a place). Both were columns saying the same word 52 times.

**Not asking about:** the world being mostly hidden behind the panel -- the list is meant to be put away once you have picked one, which is the last two pictures.
